# Jensen Huang Drops AI Events as Nvidia Opens Investigation


By OpenTools Team


·


November 10, 2026


Nvidia's board is investigating whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation after he admitted to an affair in a staff memo. Huang has dropped out of two AI events this week, and the uncertainty is already shaking the AI infrastructure builders rely on.


## Two AI Events, One Missing CEO


[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) CEO Jensen Huang has dropped out of two AI events this week after disclosing an affair and triggering a board investigation. Huang was set to be interviewed by an[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) executive at a private CEO forum on Monday evening, but is no longer expected to attend,[Business Insider](https://africa.businessinsider.com/news/jensen-huang-disappears-from-lineup-at-anthropic-ceo-forum-but-reappears-on/jthv5fn) reported, citing two people familiar with the matter.


He has also been pulled from the ElevenLabs Summit in New York this week, where he was scheduled for a fireside chat on "the future of AI." An ElevenLabs spokesperson confirmed to Business Insider that Huang is no longer speaking.


## The Memo, the Affair, and the Board


The withdrawal follows a Sunday memo in which Huang told staff he had been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologized to his family. "I am fully committed to[NVIDIA](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) and will work to earn back your confidence," Huang wrote, according to[Business Insider](https://africa.businessinsider.com/news/jensen-huang-disappears-from-lineup-at-anthropic-ceo-forum-but-reappears-on/jthv5fn) .


The board responded the same day. "The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," the company said in a[statement](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/statement-from-nvidia-board-of-directors) . A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the probe.


## The Alleged Spy and the Chip Connection


The investigation stems from an October report by The New York Times that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, and that U.S. authorities concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset. Megaspeed has been accused of helping restricted Chinese companies acquire[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) AI chips,[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/nvidia-jensen-huang-investigation-china-spy.html) reported.


Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised," but added that its inquiry will "examine all available information," per CNBC. Huang said in his memo that he supports the investigation and will cooperate fully.


## Wall Street Braces for Key-Man Risk


[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) 's stock dropped about 5% after Huang's admission,[the New York Post](https://nypost.com/2026/11/09/business/bill-ackman-elon-musk-back-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-after-affair-with-alleged-chinese-spy/) reported, and analysts are pricing in the risk that the executive, who has led the company for more than three decades, could step aside. "There is clearly risk that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the Board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally," Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. told[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/nvidia-launches-probe-after-report-ceo-huang-was-target-foreign-intelligence-2026-11-08/) . "This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock."


## Support, but No Clear Successor


Huang has no clear public successor, with roughly 60 direct reports and a company worth more than $4 trillion,[the New York Post](https://nypost.com/2026/11/09/business/bill-ackman-elon-musk-back-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-after-affair-with-alleged-chinese-spy/) reported. President Trump called Huang an "honorable guy," investor Bill Ackman urged the public to support Huang and his family, and Elon Musk replied "I agree" to a Sequoia partner's post calling Huang "irreplaceable for America's AI leadership," per the Post.


## Why It Matters for Builders


[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) 's GPUs are the foundation for nearly every AI model that builders train, fine-tune, and run, so any leadership instability or export-control tightening lands directly on chip pricing and availability. The U.S. already restricts exports of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to China,[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/nvidia-jensen-huang-investigation-china-spy.html) reported, and the probe is expected to deepen scrutiny of those sales.


For now, the risk is governance, not supply: a company spokesperson told CNBC that Huang "was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption." No timeline for the board's investigation has been announced.
